analysis:
Examined all supplied documentation, patches and mode metadata against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. Autopilot now documents dynamic verified inventory, default-on controller-directed downloads, adoption beyond lease expiry, placement holds and watchdog handling. Besides the consent expansion finding, no concrete implementation regression is established by these documentation units. model-autopilot.md:118–140 describes manifest/hash verification, disk reserve and publication checks; :151–168 bounds adoption/holds; :188–219 preserves native ownership fences on stalls. Integration must verify these contracts in the named Autopilot Swift files, particularly concurrent download budgeting, runtime disable/revocation, lease expiry during operations, and adoption admission preserving App Attest authorization (T-053), build binding (T-027), idle availability (T-029) and cancellation ownership (T-010). Catalog-unavailable ledger restoration (:63) also needs validation of recorded hashes and eligibility.
telemetry.md:34–43 adds closed busy/stall metadata, not request content; unchanged surrounding text preserves diagnostic-only accounting and cache-evidence separation. No supplied change weakens A-001 encryption, T-041 account scoping/at-rest protection, token custody, artifact qualification or privileged fan controls. Their implementations are not supplied. cli-reference.md's changed downloads/selection contract corroborates the authority expansion but does not prove runtime enforcement. Further source integration is needed to validate these security-relevant contracts; external coordinator policy remains trusted and platform-owned.

findings.detail: The BASE architecture limits Autopilot to explicitly consented cached models and excludes download authority. The new contract enables downloads whenever consent is already saved, with no storage/model cap by default (lines 86–100). It also expands the controllable set without a prompt or consent revision change (lines 39–45 and 70–75). Thus an operator who approved only cached builds can have controller-directed transfers consume bandwidth and disk and introduce additional controllable models without approving the expanded authority. The CLI patch confirms that saved enrollment now automatically includes these builds. Preserve the old scope for existing consent records: require an explicit, versioned opt-in for downloads and automatic inventory expansion, or default those capabilities off until renewed consent. Document this expanded operator/resource-control boundary in the threat model.
findings.title: Existing cached-model consent now authorizes default-on downloads without renewed consent
